note: Market sentiment & global flows for the overview. Fear&Greed is fetched LIVE in-browser (CNN equity index via proxy + crypto via alternative.me) with the baked value as fallback; breadth & regional flows are researched and baked (no free real-time API) and refreshed daily by the scheduled intel agent.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index closed 7,457.69 on Friday 17 July (-1.15% on the day, down ~1.6% from the 10 July weekly high of 7,575) as a semiconductor rout (SOX -11% on the month, SMH -9% over four weeks) dragged the tape. The S&P still sits above a rising 125-DMA thanks to the YTD advance, but momentum has cooled to a neutral read as leadership narrowed away from tech.

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Breadth actually broadened ex-tech — ~68.6% of the S&P sits above its 200-DMA (16 July), the highest since February — as energy, financials and industrials made new highs even while semis carved fresh lows. The offsetting new-lows in chips keep this reading neutral rather than outright strong.

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). Participation stayed reasonably broad as the rotation into energy/financials/industrials absorbed the semis unwind; the Summation Index is grinding sideways-to-higher while the short-term Oscillator dipped on the 17 July down day. A balanced, non-extreme read.

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Options demand turned defensive as US airstrikes on Iran entered a sixth day (17 July) and the semis complex sold off — put buying picked up on the geopolitical and AI-capex risk, tilting this component toward fear.

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. Volatility firmed off its early-July calm as the Iran escalation and the tech-led pullback pushed the VIX up toward/above its 50-day average — no longer the decidedly non-fearful read of a week ago; now neutral-to-fearful.

components.name: Safe-Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Treasuries outperformed as equities fell and the 10-year eased to ~4.55% (from ~4.57%) on the soft June CPI and risk-off flows, so bonds-over-stocks performance nudges this toward fear.

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. ICE BofA US HY OAS remains historically tight at ~269bp (10 July) despite the equity wobble — credit is not corroborating the equity fear, keeping this the most constructive component at neutral.

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 200-day MA
metrics.value: ~68.6% on 16 July — the highest since February and a clear broadening signal as energy, financials and industrials led. Confirms the advance is no longer semis-dependent even as chips fell (Barchart/MacroMicro $S5TH)

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
metrics.value: Estimated ~55-60% mid-July — the semiconductor rout (SMH -9% over four weeks) pulled tech below its 50-DMA while energy/financials/industrials stayed above, roughly offsetting; a precise dated $S5FI figure was not extractable this run (approximate/inferred)

metrics.label: NYSE advancers vs decliners (latest session)
metrics.value: Mixed on the 17 July down session — the S&P fell 1.15% on a semis-led decline but the Russell 2000 was nearly flat (-0.06%), so the internal was narrower at the mega-cap-tech line than the small-cap tape suggested

metrics.label: 52-week New Highs minus New Lows (NYSE)
metrics.value: Two-sided: fresh new highs in energy/financials/industrials against a cluster of new lows in semiconductors; net still modestly positive but no longer broadly one-directional (approximate — precise live counts not extractable)

metrics.label: NYSE McClellan Oscillator / Summation Index
metrics.value: Summation Index grinding sideways-to-higher on broadening ex-tech participation; the short-term Oscillator dipped on the 17 July down day but stayed off extremes (mcoscillator.com; exact daily NYMO not published in accessible sources; approximate)

metrics.label: Cumulative NYSE Advance-Decline line trend
metrics.value: Rising and near highs — the broad A-D line kept confirming the tape as leadership rotated from chips into energy/financials/industrials rather than collapsing; a healthier internal than a narrow mega-cap-only market (approximate trend read)

metrics.label: % of 11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA
metrics.value: ~73-82% (roughly 8-9 of 11 sector ETFs) as Energy, Industrials, Financials, Utilities, Health Care and Staples stayed above trend; only Technology/semis flirted with breaking below — consistent with the ~69% S5TH reading (inferred)

breadth.note: Breadth is broadening, not breaking: ~69% of the S&P sits above its 200-DMA (highest since February) even as the index fell, because leadership rotated out of semiconductors (SMH -9% in four weeks) and into energy, financials and industrials rather than collapsing. The A-D line is near highs and 8-9 of 11 sectors hold above trend. The open questions are whether the AI-capex/semis unwind deepens into the broader tape and whether the escalating US-Iran conflict (oil ~$81) turns the oil-price tailwind for energy into a growth headwind for everything else.

flows.period: Week ending 1 July 2026 (ICI weekly estimated long-term fund flows), supplemented by BofA equity client-flow trends (early July 2026). Flows are weekly and lagged; the full BofA 'Flow Show' regional EPFR breakdown was not itemized in free sources this run, so several regional lines are labeled approximate or carried.
flows.narrative: The verifiable weekly read turned risk-off at the fund level: ICI data for the week ended 1 July showed equity funds bleeding -$10.22B (domestic -$5.83B, world -$4.39B) while bond funds drew +$3.73B — a clean rotation from stocks to fixed income. BofA's client-flow work was more nuanced: institutional/hedge-fund buyers drove the first net US-equity inflow in five weeks with record inflows into Consumer Discretionary, even as Financials saw the largest outflows and commodity/gold funds stayed weak (~$5B of gold outflows across June). The net picture into mid-July: retail de-risking equities into bonds and cash, a tactical HF bid under US large-caps, and a fading gold bid — all before the 14 July soft-CPI print and the mid-month Iran escalation reshuffled the tape.

regions.note: ICI shows domestic-equity funds -$5.83B and world-equity -$4.39B for the week ended 1 July (total equity -$10.22B). BofA client data diverges: it flagged the first net US-equity inflow in five weeks, HF-led with record Consumer Discretionary buying and Financials the biggest outflow — measurement/window differences, so read the direction (rotation, dispersion), not a single figure.

A discrete European/DM weekly figure was not verifiable this run. The 2026 pro-international tilt has persisted in prior weeks; ICI's world-equity line was net negative (-$4.39B) for the week to 1 July, so the recent European inflow streak may have paused. Approximate/carried — treat as unconfirmed this week.

No discrete EM weekly figure surfaced in free sources this run. EM flows have been choppy with the firm dollar (DXY ~100.6) and the Iran/oil shock a net negative for oil-importing EM. Approximate — unconfirmed this week.

No specific weekly China figure public this run. Mainland-equity funds have been leaking as authorities manage the rally pace; the HK-tech complex remains volatile. China bond funds have stayed on an inflow trend. Approximate/carried.
A discrete Japan weekly figure was not verifiable this run; Japan-equity funds had bled for four straight weeks through early July on a weak yen. Approximate — unconfirmed this week.

Money-market funds continued to draw cash into mid-July as risk appetite cooled and parked yield near ~3.6-3.75% at the fed funds floor stayed attractive; a precise weekly MMF figure was not itemized this run (the prior week to 2 July saw a +$56.4B surge). Approximate.

ICI bond funds drew +$3.73B for the week ended 1 July as the rotation from equities into fixed income continued. HY OAS stayed historically tight (~269bp), so the bid is broad-based rather than a flight strictly to quality; the 10-year eased to ~4.55% on the soft June CPI.

Gold/commodity funds were the weakest cohort, shedding roughly $5B across June per BofA, and the fading ETF bid showed up in price — spot gold slipped below $4,000 to ~$3,970 by 17 July. Central-bank buying remains the offsetting structural demand, but the fund-flow tide turned against the metal.

movements.note: The marquee verifiable weekly rotation — retail-heavy fund flows moved out of stocks (domestic -$5.83B, world -$4.39B) and into fixed income as risk appetite cooled ahead of the CPI print and the Iran escalation.

movements.amount: Financials biggest outflow, gold ~-$5B June / record ConsDisc inflow (BofA)
movements.note: BofA client data shows hedge funds driving the first US-equity inflow in five weeks with record Consumer Discretionary buying, funded partly out of Financials and a fading gold bid — a tactical, sector-rotational move under the surface of the risk-off headline.

The gold/commodity outflow alongside bond and money-market inflows captures the mid-July de-risking that pushed silver to 8-month lows (~$56) and gold below $4,000 despite the soft CPI and the geopolitical flare.
